_comment: Machine-readable twin of PUBLISHED_PCR.md. That file is prose with a table
per release, which is right for a human and wrong for a fetch: parsing it
means regexing markdown, and a trust anchor should not depend on heading
punctuation. This file is the one clients read.
accepted_pcr0 is a LIST, not a value. Normally it holds exactly one entry.
During a rollover it holds two -- the incoming measurement and the outgoing
one -- so a client whose bundle predates the swap still accepts the enclave
instead of silently falling back to the non-attested path. That overlap is
the thing enclave-cutover.yml names as the prerequisite for ever running a
cutover unattended.
PRUNE THE OUTGOING ENTRY once the rollover is done. A stale entry here
silently re-admits a retired image, which is the failure mode an accept-list
trades for the one it removes.
History lives in PUBLISHED_PCR.md, deliberately not duplicated here.
Builds emit a Sigstore attestation over the PCR.json they produce, so the
measurement can be traced to a specific workflow run in this public repo
rather than taken on PayPerQ's word. Download PCR.json from the build
run's artifacts and run the command above.
Attestations begin with builds after 2026-09-02; earlier releases in
PUBLISHED_PCR.md predate CI entirely and were built by hand over SSM.
